svg.title: How clearway gets past Cloudflare
svg.desc: A scraper knocks; Cloudflare runs three checks (fingerprint vs User-Agent, the cf_clearance stamp, and the IP); if blocked with a 403, a real browser earns a stamp which is cached per site and reused; a residential proxy handles IP-only blocks.
svg.text: How a scraper gets past the Cloudflare “bouncer”
The knock → 3 checks → earn a stamp → reuse it — in plain language.
Asks the site for a page. That request is one “knock.”
🛡️ Step 2 — The bouncer runs three checks
👀 Looks vs. story — TLS fingerprint (real Chrome) must agree with the User-Agent
🎟️ Has a stamp? — the cf_clearance cookie means “already passed the bot test”
📍 Which street? — your IP; datacenter IPs (e.g. GitHub Actions) look suspicious
✅ Yes → you’re let in, the page comes back.
❌ Stuck (e.g. no stamp) → 403, blocked → go earn one ↓
🌐 Step 4 — Send a real browser to earn the stamp
Launch Playwright, pass the door test like a person, collect the cf_clearance stamp.
🗄️ Step 5 — Save the stamp, then just flash it
Cache it to avoid re-earning. One stamp per site — another site’s won’t work.
🔄 Re-knock wearing the stamp → back to Step 3 → ✅ let in
📍 Exception — when it’s just your IP (Check 3)
No disguise or stamp helps if your IP itself is blocked. Arrive from a
residential street instead — route through a residential proxy. clearway supports that.
